problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -6 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Determine whether $A=PD{P}^{-1}$ for some invertible matrix $P$ and a diagonal matrix $D,$ where $P$ and $D$ are both real. In the affirmative case, find a possible diagonal matrix $D.$

Determine whether $A=PDP^{-1}$ for some invertible matrix $P$ and a diagonal matrix $D,$ where $P$ and $D$ are both real. In the affirmative case, find a possible diagonal matrix $D.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine whether $D$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R.$ 

We start by computing the eigenvalues of $A.$ To do that, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 6 & 0 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 6 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )([{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +2]-12) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -10) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(\lambda -5)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1=4,$ $\lambda_2=5,$ and $\lambda_3=-2.$ Since all of the eigenvalues are simple roots of the characteristic polynomial, $A$ is diagonalizable. 

We construct a diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal. Therefore, one possible matrix $D$ is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069769/assets/2f943468de2124874c2d806db25c6ca91a2df9a74902af95220e4974e5ef483b.png)

Note that the diagonal matrix $D$ is unique up to the ordering of the eigenvalues. Therefore, another possible  diagonal matrix is

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=2$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & b & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & c & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & b & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ and

- the $3$rd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

In conclusion, we get $a=2,$ $b=1,$ and $c=-2.$
